heading: Space Economy Intelligence
subheading: Launch, satellites, constellations & the post-SpaceX-IPO landscape
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Space is capital-intensive with heavy government-customer concentration. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Global space economy estimated at ~$626B in 2026; Goldman Sachs and McKinsey both project a climb to $1.8T by 2035 alongside a rising wave of sector M&A

kpis.sub: STILL BELOW POST-IPO HIGH, BUT STABILIZING
kpis.label: SPCX closed above its $135 IPO price for the first time in weeks on Aug 10 and traded near $140 by Aug 16 (52-wk range $104.83-$225.64) — still ~38% below its $225.64 post-IPO high; Musk said on the Q2 call that Starship Flight 14 (targeted end of August) will attempt to catch the ship and deliver Starlink V3 to orbit for the first time

Space Capital-tracked H1 2026 investment surpassed all of 2025; momentum carried into Q3 as Stoke Space began raising $1B (~$9B valuation) and Rocket Lab lined up $3.6B in bridge financing for its Iridium acquisition

Subscribers crossed 12M in Q2 (best quarter yet, net adds of 1.7M); SpaceX added Starlink Direct-to-Cell mobile partnerships with SoftBank, NTT DoCoMo and Spark New Zealand during the quarter, extending reach ahead of Starship's first Starlink V3 delivery flight

rows.angle: Launch monopoly economics + Starlink (12M subs, ARPU $66 stable); shares closed above the $135 IPO price for the first time in weeks on Aug 10, trading near $140 by Aug 16, still ~38% below the $225.64 post-IPO high; SoftBank/NTT DoCoMo/Spark NZ Starlink mobile partnerships signed during Q2
rows.watch for: Further lockup tranches through Dec 8, 2026 (Musk's ~6.4B shares locked until Jun 2027); Starship Flight 14 (targeted end of August) aims to catch the ship and deliver first Starlink V3 satellites to orbit; xAI cash burn weighing on consolidated results

rows.watch for: EPS missed on $8.6M of Mynaric/Motiv/Iridium deal costs; shares fell >7% after-hours as Bloomberg reported (Aug 10) fresh risk that Neutron's maiden flight could slip from Q4 2026 into 2027; Q3 guided to $250-265M

rows.angle: Raised FY26 guidance (revenue $23.2-23.7B, GAAP EPS $11.80-12.00) as missile sales accelerate and backlog climbs to $42B; spun off Rocketdyne's space propulsion/power/electronics units to AE Industrial Partners while retaining a minority stake; signed a 7-yr, ~$12B THAAD/PAC-3 propulsion framework with Lockheed Martin
rows.watch for: Further SDA/missile-tracking award flow; Rocketdyne transition execution; 2028 launch readiness for Tranche 3 satellites

private_watchlist.name: Blue Origin
private_watchlist.note: Confirmed the May 28 New Glenn pad explosion traced to the main oxygen valve on a BE-4 engine; modifications now underway at both ULA's Decatur plant and Cape Canaveral, with NASA Stennis hot-fire testing set to begin this fall. Original Pad 36 rechristened 36A; construction has begun on a second Cape Canaveral pad (36B) for the larger New Glenn 9x4. Company remains "very committed" to a return to flight by year-end.

private_watchlist.name: Firefly Aerospace
private_watchlist.note: Reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $117.7M (+659% YoY, first quarter above $100M) on a record $1.5B backlog, alongside a $92.3M net loss; quarter included a $144M NASA CLPS lunar-lander award, a $75M NASA JPL MoonFall subcontract, and a $94M Space Force radar-digitization contract.

private_watchlist.name: Stoke Space
private_watchlist.note: Began raising a fresh $1B round (Bloomberg, Aug 13) at a ~$9B valuation ex-new-money, on top of the $1.34B already raised; expanding test facilities at Moses Lake (324 acres) and activating Cape Canaveral's LC-14; first Nova liftoff still targeted for end of 2026.

bear_case.title: Capital intensity
bear_case.description: Rockets and constellations burn billions before returns — Stoke Space is now raising a further $1B on top of $1.34B already spent pre-launch; dilution is chronic among small caps (RKLB's $3.6B Iridium bridge facility, ASTS's $1B convertible notes).

bear_case.title: Government concentration
bear_case.description: Much of the sector's revenue is NASA/DoD — SDA's Golden Dome build-out is driving billions in LHX/Sierra Space awards and a fresh $397M RKLB Flatellites contract; budget shifts or program cancellations reprice backlogs fast.

bear_case.title: SpaceX absorbs the value
bear_case.description: A dominant incumbent with launch-cost leverage can compress everyone else's margins — SPCX shares needed a rebound above the $135 IPO price just to stop the bleeding and remain ~38% below their post-IPO high; xAI's AI cash burn continues to weigh on consolidated results, and Musk is now promising Starship Flight 14 will both catch the ship and deliver Starlink V3 on the same flight — a high bar.

bear_case.title: Binary mission risk
bear_case.description: One failed test or launch can halve a small-cap, or push a manifest a year: Bloomberg reported Aug 10 that Rocket Lab's Neutron — already delayed once by a tank failure — now faces fresh risk of slipping from Q4 2026 into 2027, while Blue Origin's own root-cause finding (a single BE-4 oxygen valve) shows how fast hardware failure can stall a program. SpaceX's own prospectus flags "key man" dependence on Elon Musk.

catalysts.title: Rocket Lab clears key Iridium acquisition hurdles
catalysts.description: HSR antitrust waiting period lapses, Form S-4 and FCC transfer applications filed, and a $3.6B bridge facility secured from Deutsche Bank/Wells Fargo — the ~$8B deal stays on track for a mid-2027 close.

catalysts.title: Intuitive Machines reports Q2 2026
catalysts.description: Revenue quadrupled YoY to $206M (light of the $216M estimate) but backlog hit a record $1.8B; FY guidance reaffirmed at $900M-$1B with positive adjusted EBITDA still expected.

catalysts.title: Stoke Space begins raising $1B at ~$9B valuation
catalysts.description: Fresh capital targets Nova rocket production and Cape Canaveral LC-14 activation, on top of the $1.34B already raised pre-launch.

catalysts.title: Firefly Aerospace reports record Q2 2026
catalysts.description: Revenue of $117.7M (+659% YoY) crossed $100M for the first time on a record $1.5B backlog, fresh off NASA CLPS, NASA JPL and Space Force radar-digitization awards.

catalysts.title: Rocket Lab posts record Q2 revenue but Neutron risk resurfaces
catalysts.description: Revenue hit $234.1M (+62% YoY) and backlog surged to $2.36B, but shares fell >7% after-hours as Bloomberg reported fresh risk the Neutron debut could slip from Q4 2026 into 2027.

catalysts.title: AST SpaceMobile business update
catalysts.description: 13 satellites now on orbit, revenue backlog grown to ~$1.30B, and 60+ MNO partners covering 3B+ subscribers, as the network builds toward a 2026 beta commercial launch.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: Rocket Lab
positions.note: Record Q2 revenue ($234.1M, +62% YoY) and a record $2.36B backlog confirm the core thesis, and the Iridium deal cleared its HSR antitrust waiting period with $3.6B in bridge financing secured — but Bloomberg's Aug 10 report that Neutron's maiden flight could now slip into 2027 is a genuine execution risk, so weight trims slightly rather than growing further this week.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: Raised FY26 guidance (revenue $23.2-23.7B, EPS $11.80-12.00), backlog climbed to $42B, and the Rocketdyne divestiture sharpens the remaining portfolio around prime-contractor space/missile-defense economics — real improvement, so weight moves up. Also sits in your Defense sleeve — don't double-count the exposure.

positions.name: Redwire
positions.note: A second straight quarter of records (revenue $117.1M, 27.8% gross margin, $542.1M backlog) plus $21.5M of new Stalker UAS defense follow-on orders and a narrowed net loss confirm last week's upgrade was justified, not a one-quarter fluke.

positions.name: AST SpaceMobile
positions.note: Aug 10 update showed 13 satellites already on orbit, backlog grown to ~$1.30B, and 60+ MNO partners covering 3B+ subscribers — real deployment progress. Still speculative: the $1B convertible note overhang persists and beta commercial service isn't live yet.

positions.name: Intuitive Machines
positions.note: Q2 revenue of $206M missed the $216M estimate and the loss (-$0.29/sh) was wider than expected, though backlog hit a record $1.8B and management still guides to positive full-year adjusted EBITDA; keeping this small given the miss and the ever-present binary risk of a lunar landing.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: Shares closed above the $135 IPO price for the first time in weeks on Aug 10 and traded near $140 by Aug 16 — real stabilization — but that's still ~38% below the $225.64 post-IPO high, lockup tranches keep unlocking through Dec 8, 2026, and Musk is now promising Starship Flight 14 (end of August) will both catch the ship and deliver the first Starlink V3 satellites to orbit, a high-bar test. UK investors wanting SpaceX exposure without chasing the US listing can get indirect access via Scottish Mortgage (SMT, covered on the Baillie Gifford page).

positions.name: Planet Labs
positions.note: No fresh company-specific catalyst this week — a Rwanda national-program launch and a small Scottish-government award for the German unit don't move the needle on the core question of whether earth-observation data commands a defensible price; stock round-tripped from $23.10 back to ~$24.76 on sector beta, not fundamentals.

positions.name: Iridium Communications
positions.note: Now effectively a merger-arbitrage position — the HSR antitrust waiting period lapsed Aug 12 and Rocket Lab secured a $3.6B bridge facility to fund the ~$8B acquisition (still targeted for a mid-2027 close), but deal-completion and financing risk over that timeline isn't the same risk/reward as owning a satcom operator outright; RKLB stock is the cleaner way to take the same view.
